title: Johnson & Johnson Announces MONARCH™ QUEST 3, Advancing the Latest in Robotically-Assisted Bronchoscopy
summary: Johnson & Johnson has announced U.S. 510(k) regulatory clearance for MONARCH™ QUEST 3, the newest software update for its MONARCH Platform, which is a robotically-assisted bronchoscopy system. This update aims to enhance the planning, navigation, and targeting capabilities for the early detection of lung cancer, building on continuous advancements. The MONARCH QUEST 3 also integrates with Johnson & Johnson's Polyphonic™ digital ecosystem, extending surgical intelligence beyond the procedure.

title: J&J hands lymphoma bispecific CAR T back to AbelZeta
summary: Johnson & Johnson has returned the rights to prizloncabtagene autoleucel (prizlon-cel), an investigational CAR T therapy for large B cell lymphoma, to AbelZeta Pharma. J&J initially secured these rights in 2023 for $245 million upfront, and the therapy had shown a 100% response rate in an early-stage study for relapsed or refractory large B cell lymphoma. This decision comes as J&J focuses on other areas of its CAR T portfolio, including a recent $785 million partnership with Sail Biomedicines for in vivo CAR T therapies.

title: J&J Secures $2.58B Option to Acquire Sail Biomedicines
summary: Johnson & Johnson has secured an exclusive option to acquire Sail Biomedicines for $2.58 billion, backing Sail's in vivo CAR T platform for immune-mediated diseases. This collaboration marks J&J's largest investment in in vivo cell therapy to date, aiming to develop more scalable CAR T treatments that reprogram immune cells directly inside the patient, circumventing the complex ex vivo manufacturing process. Initial payments from J&J total $785 million, with potential for more upon achieving development milestones, as Sail's lead asset, SAIL-0839, remains in preclinical development.
